## Content research and overlap decision

### Reader question

How should an engineer build and interpret an AgentSight semantic flamegraph on v1.0.31, and when should token numbers be read from `agentpprof --view tokens` versus `agentsight report token`?

### Why refresh the existing canonical

- `/guides/agent-flamegraph/` already owns the reader decision for constructing and interpreting Agent Flamegraphs. Creating another “token flamegraph” or “agentpprof” URL would split one problem across near-duplicate pages.
- `/blog/how-agentsight-reconciles-token-usage/` owns source accounting and reconciliation for `agentsight report token`. It does not own the semantic-profiler workflow, tagging method, operation stack, or reproducible flamegraph publication method.
- The refresh therefore keeps the existing canonical URL and adds a bridge between the two owners rather than duplicating either one.

### Primary-source findings added in this refresh

- AgentSight v1.0.31 `agentpprof` still directly documents local Codex and Claude Code JSONL input. Shared `agent-session` support elsewhere in the product must not be misread as automatic profiler support for every provider.
- The v1.0.31 flamegraph skill keeps three separate `< 5%` unmatched gates for prompts, sessions, and LLM calls, plus distribution diagnostics around category count, top-1/top-3 share, and normalized entropy. Catch-all tags remain explicitly discouraged.
- `agentpprof --view tokens` uses reported native-session token counts when available and otherwise bounded text estimates; very large unsafe estimates become `unknown=1` rather than an arbitrarily wide bar.
- `agentsight report token` has a different evidence pipeline. An explicit `--db` selects a saved AgentSight materialized view. With no explicit DB, the report command first selects the latest saved `agentsight-*.db` when one exists and only falls back to recent native sessions when no saved DB is available; `agentsight report --local token` forces the native-session path. Its effective-token layer selects/reconciles source rows by call key, prioritizing response-observed usage ahead of orphan response usage, Gemini CLI stdout statistics, Claude telemetry, and agent-native rows, with a separate aggregate comparison for Gemini stdout totals.
- Therefore the two tools can legitimately produce different totals when their source sets or accounting paths differ. `report token` answers source-accounting/grouping questions; `agentpprof` answers semantic-distribution questions. Neither is a provider invoice calculation.
